answer: Identity carries a rota duty, not a balance. Every identity serves one adjudication shift each nine epochs: disputes are assigned at random, rulings published within one block, and the epoch emission stays locked until the shift closes clean. Seats bind to the signing key and attendance is written to the ledger, so a farm cannot share one seat across a hundred shells: each owes its own shift, and a missed one forfeits that epoch plus a rung of weight. A knoll is not held by claiming it, a prism splits only into more shifts, and a sparrow off the rota gets no grain.
